title: Upgrade to support OpenMRS Platform 3.0
body:
Updates metadataexport so it builds against, and runs on, openmrs-core master (Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: Java 21, Jakarta EE, Spring 7, Hibernate 7). It depends on the Platform 3 upgrades of initializer (mekomsolutions/openmrs-module-initializer#338) and the other O3 modules it integrates with. Same approach as the platform 3 upgrades of calculation (openmrs/openmrs-module-calculation#19), legacyui and webservices.rest.

## Changes
- Versions:
  - Module version is now 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT, on Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT (with `openmrs-bom` imported).
  - Module dependencies move to their Platform 3 versions: initializer 3, webservices.rest 5, emrapi 4, fhir2 6, idgen 7, metadatamapping 3, addresshierarchy 4, cohort 4, tasks 3, queue 4, patientflags 4, appointments 3, billing 3 and stockmanagement 4.
- Build:
  - Java 21 with `-parameters`.
  - Lombok runs from the compiler's `annotationProcessorPaths` (`lombokVersion` property). CI builds Platform 3 modules with Java 21 and 25, and javac 25 no longer runs annotation processors it only finds on the classpath.
  - `openmrsPlatformToolsVersion` is pinned to 2.8.3 so spotless doesn't reformat untouched code.
  - The `fhir2-api-2.x` and `metadatasharing-api-2.0` test dependencies are removed.
- `javax.persistence`/`servlet` become `jakarta.*`, and the DAO uses `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate`.
- `config.xml` now sets `require_version` to 3.0.0.
- `webModuleApplicationContext.xml` referenced core's `jacksonMessageConverter` bean, which core 3.0 renamed. It now references `jacksonConverter` from core's `WebConfig`.
- Core 3.0 denies an `@Authorized` call with Spring Security's `AuthorizationDeniedException` (openmrs/openmrs-core#6544). `MetadataExportControllerAdvice` now maps `AccessDeniedException` to 401/403 too, so a denied zip download no longer answers 500, and the tests expect the new type.
- metadatasharing has no 3.0 release:
  - Its exporter is gated by `@OpenmrsProfile` and still compiles against 1.2.2.
  - A test-only `ModulesWithoutPlatform3ReleaseBeanFilter` keeps metadatasharing's beans out of the test context, because they extend the removed `serializationServiceTarget`.
  - The README lists it with the domains that are supportable but not covered.
- The README's requirements and per-domain module versions are now the Platform 3 ones.
- Tests:
  - The test hbm configuration adds the mappings appointments 3.0 and cohort 4.0 now need.
  - The `event-api` test dependency is removed. The event module has no Platform 3 release (openmrs/openmrs-module-event#33 was closed in favour of core's events), and billing 3 and emrapi 4 no longer use it.
  - `ExportPackageResourceTest` expects core's `ValidationException`, because REST 5 (RESTWS-1016) no longer validates before save.
  - The fhir2 integration tests drop the H2-only unique constraint that Hibernate 7 adds for a `@OneToOne`. The real schema doesn't have that constraint.

## Depends on
- openmrs/openmrs-core#6631 (merged). Before it, the module's test context took more than 25 minutes to load, because of the advisor-creation recursion in openmrs/openmrs-core#6630. With it the full build takes about 2 minutes.
- openmrs/openmrs-core#6544 (merged). The module now needs a core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT that includes Spring Security.
- openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest#767. Until it lands, REST answers a denied request to this module's REST resources (for example a logged-out `GET /packages`) with 500 instead of 401/403.
- openmrs/openmrs-module-idgen#140, which publishes idgen's Platform 3 line as 7.0.0-SNAPSHOT. 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT is the Platform 2.8 line on idgen's `6.x` branch.

title: Export retired metadata as full rows instead of uuid-only stubs
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'ME-5111: Replace use of deprecated isVoided' -->
<!--- 'ME-JiraIssueNumber: JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->
What

- MetadataLineExporter.writeLine writes the void/retire flag and then always calls export, so a retired row carries every column
- Remove the writeRetiredDiscriminators hook and its 12 per-domain overrides, which only re-dispatched to export or wrote a subset of it
- Stop the five concept and two drug secondary exporters from skipping retired instances
- Add DomainExporter.retiredNameClashes(...) and without(...); the ten domains whose Initializer parser falls back to a name lookup exclude retired rows that share a name with another row
- Selector no longer pulls an excluded row back in through cross-domain closure; it warns naming the referencing row and the reason
- DrugDomainExporter.candidatesFor only loads the formulary when a package names a retired drug
- Tests: ~40 line exporter tests now assert full rows; new RetiredRowsRoundTripIntegrationTest replays exported CSVs through Initializer's own parsers onto fresh and populated targets; new VisitTypeDomainExporterIntegrationTest for the name-clash exclusion; selector and DomainExporter unit tests for the new helpers
- README: retired-row behaviour under "How it works", corrected reasons for the domains that still exclude retired rows, and the name-fallback limitation

Why

- Initializer's CsvParser.shouldFill fills a retired row whose uuid the target lacks and then retires it, so a uuid-only stub failed validation on a fresh server
- Every live row referencing the stub failed too, e.g. a concept whose answer is a retired concept, taking its concept sets with it
- With names now on retired rows, Initializer's name fallback would bind a retired row to a same-named live row and retire or merge it, so those rows must stay out
- Closure previously ignored exclusions(), so an excluded row could reach the zip while the manifest said it was left out

title: Improve handling of deduplication by allowing each domain to set the de-dupe key

It's not always the case that UUIDs in OpenMRS are globally unique, especially where metadata and not data are involved. Consequently, the hard assumption being made here that we could deduplicate solely by `objA.equals(objB);` doesn't quite hold.
